issues: whether a misrepresentation about a party's future intentions (non-renewal) is actionable where the contract itself permits non-renewal
the duty of honest performance in the exercise of a contractual right, including the decision not to renew
the tort of deceit for intentional misleading during the final term of a contract
promissory estoppel or detrimental reliance as an alternative basis for relief where a party refrained from seeking alternatives in reliance on misleading statements
whether a contractual non-renewal clause operates as a bar or defence to a misrepresentation or good-faith claim
damages for lost opportunity to secure alternative commercial arrangements (reliance loss)
limitation period for claims in misrepresentation, deceit, and breach of the duty of honest performance
key_facts: distribution agreement with a non-renewal clause
other party actively misled the client about their intentions during the final year
purpose of the misleading was to prevent the client from seeking alternatives
the contract was ultimately not renewed
causes_of_action: breach of the duty of honest performance
candidate_statutes: Limitations Act, 2002 (Ontario) — limitation period and discovery rule
search_terms: good faith exercise of contractual right
needs_clarification: Which province or territory governs the contract (or is specified in its governing-law clause)? This affects the applicable limitation period and any provincial commercial legislation.
